retrieval_notes: Search discovery spans conference proceedings, arXiv and official numerical documentation.
Unsupported PDF MIME types were replaced with arXiv HTML.
ACM DOI access denied; corresponding-author institution abstract used and depth recorded.
Graph topology generation titles not treated as evidence for fixed-graph signal forecasting.
No literature performance converted into GNSS millimeter gains.

sources.title: Time Series Diffusion in the Frequency Domain
sources.claim: Frequency-domain diffusion with mirrored Fourier noise; representation bias, not guaranteed superiority on all signals.

sources.title: SpecSTG: A Fast Spectral Diffusion Framework for Probabilistic Spatio-Temporal Traffic Forecasting
sources.status: arXiv v3; preprint status used, not represented as main-conference publication
sources.claim: GFT of spatial node axis at each physical time; spectral recurrent encoder and conditional denoising.

sources.title: LSCD: Lomb–Scargle Conditioned Diffusion for Time series Imputation
sources.depth: Sections 3-4 spectrum conditioning and spectral consistency
sources.claim: Lomb–Scargle conditions time-domain diffusion from irregular observations; power spectrum alone is not an invertible state.

sources.title: Frequency-Conditioned Diffusion Models for Time Series Generation
sources.depth: Author-institution abstract and metadata only; ACM DOI page denied access
sources.claim: Frequency components modeled in the denoising backbone and fused with time-domain features.

sources.title: FIDE: Frequency-Inflated Conditional Diffusion Model for Extreme-Aware Time Series Generation
sources.claim: High-frequency inflation and block-maxima conditioning; true future block maxima excluded from GNSS forecast conditions.

sources.title: The Emerging Field of Signal Processing on Graphs: Extending High-Dimensional Data Analysis to Networks and Other Irregular Domains
sources.depth: Primary bibliographic record and graph Fourier definitions cross-checked against SpecSTG section 3
sources.claim: Graph Fourier generalizes signal analysis to irregular weighted graphs; graph frequency depends on graph structure.

sources.title: FINUFFT mathematical definitions and inverse tutorial
sources.depth: Official mathematical definitions and inverse-NUFFT tutorial
sources.claim: Nonuniform Fourier sums and adjoints do not by themselves solve or guarantee an identifiable inverse problem.
